What We Do

Full-Service Wound Care Center Revenue Cycle Management

Wound care billing requires precise debridement depth coding, wound surface area measurement confirmation, advanced wound product HCPCS coding, and prior authorization for skin substitutes and NPWT. PMEX manages every element from the wound care note to payment posted.

Debridement Coding

Selective (97597 to 97598) and non-selective (97602) debridement coded by depth and area.

Skin Substitute Billing

Skin substitute HCPCS codes billed with surface area, product name, and square centimeters.

NPWT Billing

Negative pressure wound therapy (97605 to 97608) billed per session with correct device codes.

Wound Care Supply Coding

HCPCS Level II supply codes billed for dressings, silver products, and collagen applications.

Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy

HBO (99183) billed per session with correct diagnosis and medical necessity documentation.

Prior Authorization

Skin substitutes and HBO therapy authorized before treatment begins on qualifying payers.

Sound Familiar?

Common Wound Care Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Debridement billed at incorrect depth level when wound base documentation supports a deeper code.

PMEX confirms debridement depth from the wound care note and applies the correct CPT code per the documented tissue level.

Wound surface area not measured and documented, preventing correct square centimeter billing.

PMEX flags wound encounters without documented surface area measurements and confirms dimensions before the skin substitute claim is submitted.

Skin substitute product name and HCPCS code not matched, generating billing and payer edit errors.

PMEX maintains a current skin substitute HCPCS code reference and confirms the correct product code for each specific product applied.

NPWT device and dressing codes not billed separately when both are separately reimbursable.

PMEX bills NPWT device codes and dressing supply codes separately on every NPWT encounter where both are documented.

Prior authorization not obtained for skin substitutes before application.

PMEX manages skin substitute prior authorization with wound staging documentation before the product is applied.

HBO therapy session billed without confirming the qualifying diagnosis is on the coverage list.

PMEX confirms the HBO covered diagnosis before billing each session and manages the required treatment plan documentation.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Wound Care Billing

Wound care centers lose 18 to 30 percent of revenue to debridement depth errors, skin substitute authorization gaps, and surface area documentation failures.

PATTERN 01

Skin Substitute Denied, Prior Authorization Not Obtained

Acellular dermal matrix applied to a diabetic foot ulcer. Commercial payer requires prior authorization for skin substitutes above a specific cost threshold. Product applied without confirmed auth. $1,200 product claim denied. No retroactive auth available.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX manages skin substitute prior authorization before the product is applied, with wound staging documentation, conservative treatment history, and product selection rationale submitted to the payer. Auth is confirmed in the billing system before the application date.

PATTERN 02

Debridement Coded at Wrong Depth

Wound debridement performed to subcutaneous tissue level (97597). Billing team submits 97602 (non-selective, $45). Selective debridement to subcutaneous tissue (97597, $110) is the correct code. $65 per wound care session under-coded from a depth classification error.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX confirms debridement depth from the wound care note, distinguishing selective (97597 to 97598) from non-selective (97602) debridement, and applying the correct code per the documented tissue level reached during the debridement.

PATTERN 03

Skin Substitute Area Not Documented, Claim Denied

Skin substitute applied to a 6 cm x 4 cm venous ulcer. Claim submitted. Payer denies: wound surface area not documented in the procedure note. Without the documented dimensions, the correct square centimeter billing cannot be confirmed.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews wound care notes for surface area documentation before submitting skin substitute claims. When dimensions are absent, the coding team flags the note for physician addendum before the claim is released.

Questions

Wound Care Billing Questions Answered

Selective debridement is billed with 97597 (first 20 sq cm) and 97598 (each additional 20 sq cm). Non-selective debridement uses 97602. The code is determined by the debridement method and depth documented in the wound care note.

Wound dimensions (length by width in centimeters), wound staging, product name and HCPCS code, and prior authorization from the payer. We confirm all documentation is complete before submitting skin substitute claims.

Yes. The NPWT device code and the dressing supply code are separately reimbursable when both are documented. We bill both on every NPWT encounter.

Medicare covers HBO for conditions including diabetic lower extremity wounds, chronic refractory osteomyelitis, compromised grafts and flaps, and other specific diagnoses. We confirm the diagnosis is on the covered list before billing each HBO session.

We obtain prior authorization before the product is applied, with wound staging documentation, conservative treatment history, and the product cost justification required by the payer.

Within 30 days, with debridement coding workflows, skin substitute authorization tracking, and supply HCPCS coding active from day one.
